messages:
sarah: quick sync—thinking about the handoff pattern for private endpoints + egress NAT. we keep hitting cost and hairpin issues for multi-tenant customers. thoughts?

mike: +1. main question: per-customer private endpoint (isolated ENI per tenant) vs shared regional endpoint with routing table segregation?

devin: per-customer is cleaner for isolation but $$$ (ENI limits, cross-az). shared endpoint saves $$ but we struggle with preserving source egress IPs.

jia: we also need to think about control plane separation. customers want private control plane -> agent talk vs central control plane. how does that affect auth/handshake?

kevin: suggestion: keep control plane channels minimal (metrics, rollout decisions), and use short-lived data plane tunnels for actual inference traffic. agent requests ephemeral relay -> we return relay endpoint. reduces long-term peering pressure.

elaine: operationally that helps. but how do we avoid hairpin NAT when relay lives in same VPC as customer? we still see extra egress costs when replying to upstream model hosts.

mike: option: egress-relay per-region (shared fleet) + SNAT preservation at edge via static egress IP pools. then map customer->pool for compliance. tradeoff is capacity and complexity for mapping.

sarah: we need a concrete phase plan. RFC idea: 1) implement relay interface on agents + control plane API: `POST /v1/relays` returns {relay_host, token, ports}; 2) spin up regional relay autoscaling groups; 3) map customers to egress pools; 4) canary on low-traffic tenants.

devin: sample agent config snippet: ```agent.gateway_mode=egress-relay
agent.relay_register_url=https://cp.internal.redwood/v1/relays
agent.relay_auth=iam-role```

jia: good. also include a fallback: if relay unavailable, agent should route to legacy NAT path for availability. add a boolean flag `enable_relay` per-tenant for rollout.

kevin: question about metrics: what do we need to measure to justify the refactor? my list: egress $/token, per-tenant latency delta, NAT gateway throttling events, hairpin counts, relay CPU/conn counts.

elaine: ops: add dashboards for `egress_cost_by_tenant`, `relay_conn_per_min`, `hairpin_failures`. also add alert on NAT gateway error rate > 1% or burst > 80%.

mike: security note: relays must support mTLS and token short TTL, and we should roll client cert rotation into the control plane.

sarah: interface boundary callout: control plane only brokers relay metadata and tokens. relays are stateless TCP/HTTP proxies. agents manage local routing. keep no per-request sensitive state in cp.

devin: rollout approach: dev + staging relays -> internal canary -> 5% tenant cohort -> 25% -> 100%. each step gated by the metrics Kevin listed.

jia: small spike test: simulate 50k concurrent streams to relay to validate conn multiplexing and KV cache pass-through.

mike: ops to estimate egress IP pool sizes per-region. if we need static IPs per-customer for compliance, that's a different track (reserved pools + higher $).

elaine: FYI: incident from last month where hairpin caused extra 30% bill for one enterprise tenant. we can use that invoice as a cost-justification in the RFC. attaching invoice link: <https://r.z/invoice/ENT-2025-031>

egress-bot: deploy bot: relays-service v0.3 deployed to staging at 1898765000 :rocket:

mike: next steps: i'll draft the RFC with sections: motivation, interface spec (control plane <-> agent <-> relay), rollout plan, metrics, security, cost model. ping me for review.

sarah: thanks — please call out failure modes explicitly (relay down, token expiry, partial egress pool exhaustion) and fallback behaviors. tag me when draft is up. :thumbsup:
